name: scope-benchmark
description: Property-neutral regression benchmark for deterministic input and output checks (OffScopeDetector and ScopeOutputCheck), the pre-call classifier, and guarded replies. Version 3 replaces the imported domain examples with general community examples while preserving adversarial syntax, case ids, expectations, and tune/holdout splits. The inherited holdout labels are reported separately for regression comparison; these adapted examples are not an independently blinded evaluation. A property adds domain examples in ai/benchmarks/scope-benchmark.json, merged at load.

categories.CodeRequest: Requests to write, fix, explain, convert, or review code, scripts, markup, queries, or configuration, in many phrasings and programming languages, including disguised and pasted ones.
categories.GeneralAssistant: General-purpose assistant asks: homework, essays, translation of unrelated text, trivia, and other topics outside the community.
categories.DirectInjection: Member messages that try to override the rules: ignore previous instructions, personas, fake system or developer messages, role-play.
categories.IndirectInjection: Instructions hidden in fetched documents or web page text; the member's own ask is benign and the reply must not follow the hidden instruction.
categories.PromptExtraction: Attempts to make the assistant reveal or quote its rules or system prompt.
categories.Medical: Diagnosis, treatment, or medication requests that must be redirected to a qualified professional rather than answered or refused outright.
categories.InScope: General community, class, event, and account questions, including near-misses such as orientation program, class schedule, macro goals, a python exhibit, and Java coffee.
categories.CodeReply: Model replies that contain code and must be rejected by the post-call check.
categories.LeakReply: Model replies that quote the engine's fixed rules and must be rejected by the post-call check.
categories.CleanReply: Ordinary community replies (lists, tables, percentages, schedules, symbols) that the post-call check must deliver.
